reaudit_note: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

RFC8050-4.1-1.note: rejudge 2026-10-02 (c33 judge): + TestRFC8050AddPathRIBEntryFollowsFigure1 compares WriteRIBEntries add-path output with the literal Figure 1 octets (Peer Index 00 03, Originated Time 5f 5e 10 00, Path Identifier 01 02 03 04, Attribute Length 00 04, attributes) and reads the same octets through DecodeRIBRecord under all four AFI/SAFI-specific add-path subtypes 8-11; - TestRIBRecordRoundTrip (base subtype 2 reads no Path Identifier). Literal octets, not a symmetric round trip, so a misplaced or mis-sized field on either side goes red. Judge break: decodeRIBEntries reading only the low 16 bits of the Path Identifier turns the new unit red in all four subtypes while HEAD TestRIBRecordAddPathRoundTrip stays green. Does not depend on add-path NLRI parsing (the RIB prefix sits in the record header, no Path ID).

RFC8050-4.2-1.note: Forbidden behaviour: reading RIB_GENERIC_ADDPATH (subtype 12) RIB Entries as redefined (a Path Identifier in each entry), or losing the Path Identifier that belongs in the raw NLRI. TestRIBGenericAddPathRoundTrip hand-builds the bytes the RFC describes (Path ID 42 at the head of the NLRI blob, then an entry with Peer Index, Originated Time, Attribute Length, attributes and no Path ID) and requires rec.NLRI == nlri and Entries[0].Attributes == attrs; a decoder that read a 4-octet Path ID from the entry would take 0x0004 plus attribute bytes as the path id and misparse the attribute length, so the attribute comparison or the decode goes red. The negative TestRIBGenericRoundTrip requires the base subtype 6 NLRI to decode verbatim. Ze writes no subtype 12 record (internal/mrt/encode.go writes none; internal/mrt/decode.go is the only producer), so the decode path is the whole surface.

RFC8050-x-1.note:
RFC 8050 §2: "The Advertisement of Multiple Paths [RFC7911] extension for BGP alters the encoding of the BGP Network Layer Reachability Information (NLRI) format for withdraws and announcements. Therefore, new BGP4MP/BGP4MP_ET subtypes as defined in [RFC6396] are required to signal to an MRT parser how to parse the NLRI." RFC 7911 §5 supplies the directional condition: "For a BGP speaker to be able to send multiple paths to its peer, that BGP speaker MUST advertise the ADD-PATH Capability with the Send/Receive field set to either 2 or 3, and MUST receive from its peer the ADD-PATH Capability with the Send/Receive field set to either 1 or 3, for the corresponding <AFI, SAFI>."

Q1: Yes within the carriers' stated scopes. TestRFC8050MessageCallbackPreservesEncodingAndFraming asserts exact BGP4MP/BGP4MP_ET types, received/LOCAL subtypes 9/11 versus 4/7, original complete bytes and record count for isolated classic announcements, classic withdrawals, MP_REACH and MP_UNREACH. Its contexts are explicitly registered by the test, not derived through the live Peer. TestMRTWinningCollisionPreservesOPEN now adds a real Peer and TCP collision handoff: four original OPENs under 7/4/7/4, exactly one unchanged incoming and outgoing mixed withdrawal, subtypes 9/11, exact classic and MP prefixes, and exact Path Identifiers only in each negotiated family. It contains no announcement UPDATE.

Q2: The exact assertions discriminate wrong subtype selection and byte loss within those exercised cases, but the composite still cannot detect a wrong directional context at the receive observer boundary. [INFERENCE from source, not an executed mutant] Replacing s.recvCtxID with s.sendCtxID only in session_wire.go::observeReceivedWire leaves the callback carrier unaffected because it enters at notifyWireMessage. In the collision carrier, both supplied UPDATEs contain classic and MP withdrawals. The correct receive context enables IPv6 and the wrong send context enables IPv4; dump.go::updateAddPath ORs the families, so either context still yields subtype 9 for the incoming mixed UPDATE. The original bytes remain unchanged. Its offline prefix/ID assertions use SessionContexts.ObserveMessage and BGPMessage.AddPathFor, which independently recover the correct modes from captured OPENs, rather than validating the context supplied to the recorder. Those assertions therefore do not expose this observer-context substitution. A later single-family received UPDATE would be mislabeled under that substitution. This is an unproven boundary, not an allegation that current production code makes the substitution.

Q3: Yes for the asserted behavior. The callback fixture isolates each NLRI location and the collision fixture uses actual, structurally valid mixed withdrawals and asymmetric directional OPEN capabilities. Announcements in the callback fixture are raw-observer framing fixtures, not proof of successful semantic route acceptance; that distinction does not invalidate their MRT subtype assertions because recording precedes semantic validation. The collision test's transport and original-OPEN assertions establish reachability and epoch fidelity, while subtype and decoded-prefix assertions supply the bounded semantic evidence.

Q4: No for whole-stack directional signaling. The new carrier closes the previous absence of live mixed-withdrawal and original-OPEN evidence, but every discriminating live UPDATE still expects an ADDPATH subtype. The only base-subtype negative cases inject their context below the live context-selection boundary. Composite evidence therefore still lacks a live case whose expected subtype changes when the observer uses the opposite directional context. Announcement subtype checks exist at the callback boundary; the new withdrawal carrier must not be described as live mixed-announcement proof.

Polarity: The old positive and negative tags describe genuinely distinct table cases, not the same assertion counted twice. The negative is forbidden false ADDPATH labeling of ordinary-family input, not malformed-input rejection. The new positive tag is accurate and bounded; it does not add a live negative control. Preserve weak rather than treating OPEN-backed reader decoding as proof of correct writer-side context selection.

RFC8050-x-2.note: rejudge 2026-10-02 (c33 judge): {single-polarity: positive} (Figure 1 has no alternative encoding to refuse). TestRFC8050AddPathRIBEntryFollowsFigure1 pins the 32-bit field in network order by literal octets 01 02 03 04 on write and value 0x01020304 on read; four distinct octets and a value above 0xFFFF expose a 16-bit width or a reversed order. Judge break: a 16-bit read of the field turns it red, HEAD TestRIBRecordAddPathRoundTrip (PathID 1 and 2) stays green, which was the earlier gap.

RFC8050-x-3.note: Independent final source rejudgment after formatting. RFC 8050 section 3: "The fields of these message types are identical to the equivalent non-additional-path versions specified in Section 4.4 of [RFC6396]. These enhancements continue to encapsulate the entire BGP message in the BGP message field." Read the full section and RFC 6396 section 4.4 base layouts, all four tagged carriers and actual producers. Q1 yes collectively: internal/mrt/rfc8050_layout_test.go::TestRFC8050AddPathBGP4MPRecordsKeepTheBaseFields feeds independently literal records through ReadFrom for subtypes 8/9/10/11, checks every base header field and all 45 UPDATE octets, and compares base-subtype readings. internal/mrt/mrt_test.go::TestBGP4MPMessageRoundTrip checks preserved fields and the complete literal Path-ID-bearing UPDATE. internal/plugins/mrt/rfc8050_addpath_record_test.go::TestRFC8050AddPathRecordAddsNoFieldToTheBaseLayout calls the actual recorder in both directions and asserts exactly two records, each byte after its timestamp, subtype 9/11, length 65, exactly 20 base-header octets and the complete 45-octet UPDATE. Q2 yes for those exact independent reader/writer assertions: lifting the Path Identifier into an extra MRT field, shifting fields or dropping/reconstructing message octets fails. The supplementary internal/mrt/mrt_test.go::TestBGP4MPStateChangeRoundTrip is only a roundtrip control over the shared header and cannot alone prove absence of a newly inserted field; its negative tag does not establish an independent adversarial ADDPATH case. Q3 yes for the effective carriers: a complete framed UPDATE containing a real Path Identifier isolates the temptation to add an MRT field; expected record length and all expected octets are independent of production encoders. The writer negative asserts forbidden output absence, not malformed-input rejection. Q4 yes collectively for unchanged fields and complete encapsulation; the weak state-change control is not used to confer that credit. internal/mrt/encode.go::WriteBGP4MPMessage/writeBGP4MPCommon and decode.go::DecodeBGP4MPMessage/decodeBGP4MPHeader implement the common layout, and internal/plugins/mrt/component.go::OnBGPMessage copies the complete original frame. Formatting the plugin carrier changes no assertion or expected octet. This is source judgment only; no discrimination renewal or test run is claimed.

RFC8050-x-4.note:
Independent source rejudgment of all 12 current RFC8050-x-4 tagged carriers and 19 claims, including five newly enrolled units and the subsequently narrowed session-context positive claim. RFC8050 §2 states: “MRT parsers are usually stateless. In order to parse BGP messages that contain data structures that depend on the capabilities negotiated during the BGP session setup, the MRT subtypes are utilized.” “Usually” does not prohibit actual OPEN evidence. RFC7911 §3 states: “In order to carry the Path Identifier in an UPDATE message, the NLRI encoding MUST be extended by prepending the Path Identifier field, which is of four octets.” RFC7911 §5 states: “For a BGP speaker to be able to send multiple paths to its peer, that BGP speaker MUST advertise the ADD-PATH Capability with the Send/Receive field set to either 2 or 3, and MUST receive from its peer the ADD-PATH Capability with the Send/Receive field set to either 1 or 3, for the corresponding <AFI, SAFI>.” RFC8050 §3 additionally states: “These enhancements continue to encapsulate the entire BGP message in the BGP message field.” These support per-family directional decoding from actual captured negotiation, not rewriting or splitting mixed UPDATEs, inventing missing OPENs, or imposing a universal subtype/OPEN-conflict refusal rule.

Q1: substantially yes for the bounded assertions, not for universal subtype-only decoding. TestIsAddPathHelpers classifies listed subtype hints; its negative prose must not be generalized into proof that decoding never consults negotiation. TestRFC8050AddPathBGP4MPUpdateNLRIReadBySubtype genuinely checks one no-OPEN subtype-9 classic announcement as exactly 10.0.0.0/24, but does not assert the decoded ID array. TestRFC8050SubtypeControlsEveryNLRILocation checks eight base/ADD-PATH subtypes under both MRT types, subtype hints, exact classic/MP prefixes and independently truncated identifier locations, but all decode cases have matching OPENs and exact ID values are not checked. TestRFC8050SessionContextDecodesMixedDirections checks four distinct prefixes, IDs 0x01020304/0x05060708, ordinary-family ID absence, missing/one-sided/repeated OPENs, teardown/notification, ASN/endpoint/interface isolation, new epochs/files, dynamic identity, post-handshake state preservation and retained immutable context. Its corrected positive claim now describes those decoded-value assertions accurately; it makes no full-byte preservation claim.

TestRFC8050CommandsReadSubtypeContext checks OPEN-backed homogeneous show/density counts of two announcements and two withdrawals plus AS_PATH content matching. Its narrow-header cases explicitly force four-byte AS_PATH parsing in the content helper, so they do not prove RFC6396 AS_PATH-width compliance. TestRFC8050CommandsRequireMixedContext checks both mixed arrangements through show/density/filter, preserves OPENs through filtering, and requires unavailable-context errors without the prelude, including AS-path, attributes and communities commands. TestRFC8050MessageCallbackPreservesEncodingAndFraming checks isolated classic/MP announcement/withdrawal locations, both directions and MRT types, exact record count/subtype and original bytes. It injects its registered context through notifyWireMessage; it is not a real handshake, and its no-OPEN parse-success assertions do not check decoded prefix/ID values or explicitly decode MP NLRI.

The new TestMRTMigrationEpochUsesActualLocalOPEN checks real TCP Bad Peer AS/fallback, three original OPENs, actual fallback LocalAS, original mixed withdrawal bytes and exact directional prefixes/IDs, including a retained outbound writer after Session.transport and the fallback flag change. Its standalone Session explicitly publishes IDs derived from actual negotiation; automatic Peer publication is not established by this unit alone. TestMRTWinningCollisionPreservesOPEN and TestMRTCollisionWinnerReservation use the real Reactor/Peer lifecycle, retain the same winning TCP connection and noncanonical original OPENs, check OPEN directions 7/4, require exactly one original mixed withdrawal in each direction under subtypes 9/11, and assert exact classic/MP prefixes and IDs with ordinary-family IDs absent. Reservation exercises both published and taken/pre-install handoff barriers before those same semantic assertions. These carriers prove withdrawals, not announcements; neither their reservation algorithm nor third-arrival EOF is an RFC8050 mandate.

TestMRTEmptyMPFamilyRequiresContext checks recorder subtype 9 and original bytes for ordinary classic NLRI plus an empty IPv6 MP_UNREACH. Without OPENs parsing returns ErrContextUnavailable and six semantic commands return nonzero. Literal directional OPENs make the identical bytes decode exactly 10.0.0.0/24 and the intentional 0.0.0.0/0 with no classic IDs; density succeeds. Recorder context is injected, but reader negotiation is obtained from literal OPENs. The command negative promises nonzero status, not separately pinned diagnostics or positive controls for all six commands. TestMRTContextCapabilityASNBoundaries crosses eleven identity cases with peer/local and sent/received dimensions. Valid capability-derived identities, including narrow AS_TRANS representation, preserve original UPDATE bytes, all four exact prefixes and IDs; wrong wide AS_TRANS, low-word aliases and capability/MyAS mismatches return ErrContextUnavailable. This is negotiation-association evidence, not whole RFC6793 or AS_PATH-width proof.

Q2: these bounded exact-value/error assertions can detect the behaviors they name; whole-row subtype-directed decoding remains unproven. Live observation retains connection-owned ASN/transport and directional context through dispatchObservedWire -> notifyWireMessage -> OnBGPMessage. updateAddPath examines families actually present, including empty MP fields; its OR is a record-level hint, not a family-wide decoding mode. Collision ownership passes the socket, parsed OPEN and original bytes through the Peer slot to runOnce -> acceptWithOpen, releasing the reservation after acceptance. Reader dispatch explicitly routes all eight message subtypes and observes OPEN evidence before semantic callbacks. ObserveMessage associates capability-derived ASN identities and immutable directional negotiation; AddPathFor uses negotiation when present and the subtype otherwise; updateContext refuses multiple-family ambiguity without negotiation. Both analysis reader paths retain the context, and the six exercised semantic command consumers propagate decoding failure rather than silently counting or filtering it away.

The parent's completed native output and canonical rfc/discrimination/rfc8050.json show seven newly added x-4 route-revert records, halting dispatchObservedWire, acceptWithOpen, takeInboundConnection, AddPathFor, updateContext and openASNMatches (both polarities). These establish reachability under the named whole-body panic, not targeted semantic mode/identity/reservation discrimination. Both ASN records fail in the first valid largest-two-octet/peer/received case; their negative record does not independently demonstrate discrimination against a bad identity. takeInboundConnection can halt before any collision handoff. The subsequent session-context claim correction requires its renewed records; their completion/freshness is not asserted by this source judgment.

Q3: the meaningful mixed-direction and ASN cases have distinct expected prefixes/IDs, and unavailable-context negatives have matching OPEN-backed controls. The empty-family control intentionally contains a default route. Older homogeneous layout fixtures reuse classic/MP prefixes and are not full BGP semantic-validity evidence. No generic malformed/socket or capacity test is counted toward this row.

Q4: no. Preserve weak because the matching-OPEN prefix matrix does not exercise AddPathFor's no-negotiation branch. The one exact no-OPEN decode carrier covers only subtype 9 and one classic announcement. Classifier assertions and successful parser calls cannot supply the missing exact no-OPEN base/ADD-PATH, withdrawal and MP prefix/ID assertions. New session, collision, empty-family and identity coverage does not close that limit. This is implemented-but-incompletely-proven behavior, not an absent capability; no partial annotation authorizes a partial verdict. Subtype/OPEN disagreement remains unspecified/unproven here, not an invented mandatory rejection obligation.

Preserve separately disclosed RFC6396-4.4.3-1: RFC6396 §4.4.3 states, “The AS_PATH in these messages MUST only consist of 4-byte AS numbers.” bgp4mpTypeSubtype still selects AS4 variants while OnBGPMessage preserves original wire bytes. Actual OPEN ASN and AS_TRANS association do not establish captured AS_PATH width. This rejudgment neither closes nor changes that other row.

Read the producing and consuming boundaries: reactor buildOpen/sendOpen/openLocalAS; connectionEstablished and setSendCtxID; observeReceivedWire, observedBGPWriter.Write/observe, dispatchObservedWire and notifyWireMessage; Peer collision slot/reservation transfer and runOnce/acceptWithOpen/processOpen; Established setEncodingContexts; recorder OnBGPMessage/updateAddPath/bgp4mpTypeSubtype; capability.Negotiate's directional calculation; MRT subtype classifiers, WriteBGP4MPMessage/writeBGP4MPCommon, DecodeBGP4MPMessage, readRecords/dispatchBGP4MP, ObserveMessage/ObserveState/openEvidence/openASNMatches/AddPathFor/updateContext, ParseBGPMessage/parseUpdate/parsePrefixesAFI and MP parsers; analyze processMRTFile/readMRTRecords, show/count/density, filter/content matching, and AS-path/attributes/communities error consumers. All 12 tagged test bodies and their relevant helpers were read. No tests, builds, native actions or edits were performed by this auditor; parent owns audit-stamp, record renewal and final freshness verification.

Issues: no patch-introduced bug found. Retain the exact no-OPEN coverage limit and classifier-only interpretation. Remove the resolved session-context full-byte-wording issue. No other row is rejudged and no protocol expansion is authorized.
